identity.title: Invalidate qualified results when the current Recipe, inputs, or SDK identity changes

origin.kind: scheduled 2D task execution and current-source owner audit
origin.summary: 2D-025 asked whether an old Good/Bad qualification could still look current after a Recipe parameter, same-filename input, dependency, or loaded SDK/runtime change. The existing immutable snapshot owner was reused before adding the smallest current-identity projection.

state.current_summary: The existing QualifiedRecipeSnapshotStore remains the immutable payload owner. Recipe Manager now compares the selected current Recipe/Pipeline bytes, actual input/dependency bytes and ordered Validation Set identity, and the loaded SDK/runtime path/version/size/SHA set. Any required difference is stale and Verify fails closed; historical payload/evidence remains readable and no approval is restored without explicit re-evaluation.

objective.summary: Audit and enforce current identity/stale policy for qualified Recipe results without creating a second qualification system.
constraints: Reuse QualifiedRecipeSnapshotStore, QualifiedRecipeSnapshotPreflight, existing Validation Set storage, and the Recipe Manager controller call path.
Do not delete or rewrite historical payloads/reports, auto-revoke lifecycle state, or make working copies inherit qualification.
Keep fixtures, generated evidence, and test outputs on D:\OpenVisionLab-TestData\OpenVisionLab_Dev; do not modify C:\Git\2D\Original, hardware, user data, or external services.
Do not commit, push, release, deploy, or perform external communication.

criteria.text: Reopening an unchanged immutable Snapshot accepts the same Recipe/input/dependency/runtime identity.
A current Recipe/Pipeline parameter, same-filename input bytes, or SDK/runtime replacement difference is stale; Verify and preflight creation do not restore the previous qualification.
Historical payload/evidence remains readable while stale, and the existing working-copy boundary remains qualification-free.

context.location: QualifiedRecipeSnapshotStore owns immutable manifest/inventory/archive verification; OpenVisionRecipeQualifiedSnapshotController owns Recipe Manager qualification projection; RecipeCommandSurface supplies the selected current Recipe/Pipeline/Validation Set context.

RecipeCommandSurface contextual List/Verify -> OpenVisionRecipeQualifiedSnapshotController.EvaluateCurrentIdentity -> QualifiedRecipeSnapshotStore.Verify plus current Pipeline, Validation Set source/dependency, and runtime fingerprint comparison.

Any required current identity difference is displayed as Qualification stale and Verify fails closed. Payload/evidence is not deleted, and explicit re-evaluation is required before a current qualification is accepted.

The current WPF target was rebuilt but stopped before Snapshot creation at the existing Batch row stored-source preflight; stale visual rendering, full theme/DPI, hardware, release, and Original repository mutation remain outside this evidence.

artifacts.summary: Owner map, current identity/stale policy, acceptance matrix, verification, and WPF preflight boundary.
Debug/Release qualified snapshot smoke outputs and WPF target recheck outputs.

evidence.observation: The focused Debug smoke passed same-identity reopen, Recipe edit stale, input-byte edit stale, SDK replacement stale, historical evidence readability, and re-evaluation-before-new-Snapshot checks.
The same focused smoke passed against the Release binary with the same stale/current identity matrix.
Debug and Release builds completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors after the current-identity change; the targeted diff check reported no whitespace errors.

The WPF target was rebuilt successfully but both fresh runs stopped before Snapshot creation with `BLOCKED | Batch row 1: stored source snapshot is missing or changed.` The failure is in the existing batch source-artifact preflight; no visual stale-state claim is made.

events.summary: 2D-025 current Recipe/input/dependency/runtime identity is fail-closed through the existing qualification owner; historical evidence remains readable and the WPF fixture limitation is recorded rather than bypassed.
